image.alt: Meta shares slide over 2% on Monday: here's why

children: Meta Platforms META shares fell about 2.4% on Monday, extending a multiweek decline for the Facebook parent.
The stock has lost roughly 12% over the past month as investors weigh its rising debt load and growing concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom.
The decline comes amid aggressive borrowing to finance AI investments and mounting legal pressures.
The broader market also remained under pressure, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq slipping more than 2%.
Meta continues to spend big
In early November, Meta completed approximately $25 billion in bond sales, comprising a $15 billion dollar-denominated offering and a €9 billion euro bond sale.
The borrowing comes as Meta ramps up investment in data centers and AI infrastructure, with its 2026 capital expenditure guidance standing at $135 billion to $145 billion.
The latest issuance adds to the company's approximately $84 billion in outstanding debt as of September 30.
The concerns follow Meta's third-quarter results, reported in October.
Revenue rose 26% year over year to $64.60 billion, but free cash flow turned negative at $2.12 billion as heavy spending continued. A large legal charge also weighed on profits.
Legal risks add to investor concerns
Legal pressures are also playing a part.

Italy's data protection authority fined Meta €805 million, approximately $887 million, over its access to photos, videos and related metadata in the galleries of Android users through a Facebook feature.
The regulator said approximately 20 million users in Italy could be affected. Meta strongly disagreed with the findings and said it would appeal.
Separately, a coalition of nonprofits filed a lawsuit in San Francisco seeking an injunction against Meta and other major AI developers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceX entities.
The complaint argues that rapid AI advancement creates catastrophic risks and seeks restrictions on the development and deployment of more advanced AI models.
The lawsuit adds to growing scrutiny of the AI industry and the potential regulatory challenges facing companies investing heavily in frontier models.
JPMorgan adds Meta to its focus list
Despite the concerns surrounding Meta's spending and legal exposure, Wall Street remains constructive on the company's longer-term growth prospects.
JPMorgan added Meta shares to its focus list last week, citing the potential for AI to strengthen its advertising business and create new revenue opportunities.

“We see continued strong revenue growth for Meta on AI-driven ad improvements, & we are bullish on Muse expansion & monetization potential, along w/the enterprise opportunity for Meta Model API & Muse Code,” the brokerage said.
The assessment suggests that JPMorgan sees opportunities beyond Meta's core advertising business, particularly as it expands its AI products and enterprise offerings.
The broader technology and AI sector also remained under pressure on Monday amid continued fallout from the leadership controversy and resignation at Nvidia.
Uncertainty surrounding the chipmaker has weighed on related stocks as investors reassess AI spending plans and supply-chain risks.
